questionAnswered: Yes: the built first-party wrapper stack can host and run a real Foldkit app under happy-dom. `embed` from @role-model-router/foldkit/runtime mounts the app into a real DOM container, a DOM click dispatches the Message through the runtime and re-renders, a second control rendered through @role-model-router/foldkit-ui works, and dispose removes the DOM and restores the container without throwing.

mountApi.used: Runtime.embed(makeApplication({ Model, init, update, view, container })) from @role-model-router/foldkit/runtime
mountApi.handle: EmbedHandle { ports, dispose }; dispose is idempotent and restores the container (vendor/foldkit/packages/foldkit/src/runtime/hostConnector.ts:61-74, src/runtime/start.ts:186-286).
mountApi.whyNotRun: `run` returns void (src/runtime/start.ts:106-130) and has no host-controlled unmount, so it cannot express the required 'unmount does not throw' assertion.
mountApi.whyNotHydrate: `hydrate` adopts a server-rendered root stamped by renderToString and terminates startup when that root is absent (src/runtime/start.ts:150-184); this slice has no server render, so hydration is not the honest entry here.
mountApi.whyNotHandRolledUpdateLoop: No update loop is hand-rolled. The test only drives the real runtime through a DOM click; the click path is DOM event -> h.OnClick -> Message -> update -> patch.
mountApi.lifecycleFinding: While mounted, the runtime replaces the configured container element with the rendered root in the DOM and, on interrupt/dispose, removes the rendered tree and puts the original container back empty (src/runtime/renderer.ts:273-298). The test therefore asserts against document.body while mounted and against document.getElementById('s14a-app-shell') === container with 0 children after dispose.
mountApi.preconditionFinding: makeApplication/makeElement require the container to carry an id for Model preservation across reloads and refuse to start otherwise (src/runtime/runtime.ts:371, :392-393). The test sets container.id before mount; the first RED after implementing the app was exactly this refusal.

shape: Model is an Effect Schema.Struct of { theme: 'light' | 'dark' (Schema.Literals), clicks: Schema.Number } - BaseApplicationConfig requires Model: Schema.Codec (src/runtime/makeApplication.ts:33).
Message is defineMessageUnion({ Clicked, ToggledTheme }) - a { _tag: string } union (makeApplication.ts:180-182; typing-game/client/src/message.ts:7-16).
update is a pure (model, message) => { model } with no Commands (src/update/update.ts:37-44; typing-game/client/src/update.ts:95-113).

view is (model, h: HtmlBuilder<Message>) => Document and threads the runtime-supplied h as a parameter; it is never stored (src/html/index.ts:5520-5545; typing-game/client/src/view/view.ts:15-60). The Document body mounts the accepted RM3 primitive (@role-model/ui/foldkit-button) plus a second control rendered through @role-model-router/foldkit-ui/button.
mount.ts keeps makeApplication and embed separate so the program and the host handle are both inspectable; no React import anywhere in the package.
dependencies: @role-model-router/effect-platform-browser workspace:* (the built foldkit runtime resolves it from its own package; declared here for the app's stack coherence)
@role-model/ui workspace:* (extra beyond the three named wrappers; required to mount the accepted RM3 primitive)
appShape.tsconfigDeviation: module/moduleResolution are ESNext/Bundler instead of the base NodeNext. Reason: the app imports @role-model/ui/foldkit-button source, whose relative import style is bundler-style (no .js extension); NodeNext rejects it, and the ui package's own project typecheck is already blocked by a pre-existing TS6059. Bundler resolution is also what a Vite-hosted app uses. NoEmit is on; include is src only.
appShape.tsconfigPathsShim: compilerOptions.paths maps `foldkit` and `foldkit/*` to ../../packages/foldkit/dist/types/*. This works around a wrapper defect: @role-model-router/foldkit-ui's emitted .d.ts files still import the upstream bare name `foldkit/...` (57 occurrences; e.g. dist/types/button/index.d.ts) even though its JS imports were rewritten to @role-model-router/foldkit. Reported as a follow-up; the JS/runtime graph is unaffected.

red.name: setup RED
red.observed: Failed to resolve import "../src/mount" from "test/mount.test.ts". Does the file exist? (app entry did not exist yet).

red.name: mount precondition RED
red.observed: [foldkit] Runtime container must have an `id` for Model preservation across reloads... then the test timed out waiting for the button. Fix: container.id = 's14a-app-shell'.

red.name: render RED (wrong foldkit-ui import)
red.observed: [foldkit] Application crash: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'view') at view.ts:23 - the ./button subpath exports `view`, not a `Button` namespace. Fix: import { view as uiButtonView }.

red.name: behavioural RED (required form)
red.observed: Deliberately removed the primary button's onClick: 1 failed -> 'Timed out waiting for the counter to update after the primary click' with the rendered body still showing 'Clicks: 0'. Restored afterwards.

green.command: cd role-model-router/apps/runtime-ui-next && vitest run (package vitest.config.ts sets environment: happy-dom, include test/**/*.test.ts)
assertions: RM3 primary button rendered into the DOM with the RM3 classes (h-[36px], rounded-[var(--rm-radius-field)]) and the accessible text 'Clicked 0 time(s)'
primary.click() dispatches Message.Clicked through the runtime: after the patch the body shows 'Clicks: 1' and the button text 'Clicked 1 time(s)'
the foldkit-ui theme toggle renders and dispatches Message.ToggledTheme: body switches to 'Dark shell'
handle.dispose() does not throw, a second dispose() does not throw (idempotent), the container is restored in the DOM with 0 children, and the rendered text is gone

typecheck.note: Passes with the paths shim described above. This is a clean typecheck of the new package; it does not typecheck the app's test file (tsconfig include is src/**/*.ts).

registers.git: The package is a new untracked directory (no commit). Its node_modules is gitignored (.gitignore:2).

workspaceWiringDoneForVerification.why: The new package needs workspace links, and the controller said it wires them; this session may not install. To run the required RED/GREEN/typecheck now, app-local node_modules junctions were created by hand: @role-model-router/foldkit, @role-model-router/foldkit-ui, @role-model-router/effect-platform-browser, @role-model/ui, effect (workspace packages) and vitest + happy-dom (from role-model-router/packages/foldkit/node_modules). No packages were fetched and no lockfile was changed.
workspaceWiringDoneForVerification.controllerActionNeeded: Run the workspace install for the new importer (frozen lockfile needs the role-model-router/apps/runtime-ui-next importer entry), then delete/replace these junctions. The app's vitest/happy-dom and typescript are not declared as devDependencies (external deps are reported, not added, per the task); CI needs a decision on whether the app declares them or reuses a workspace test setup.

unverified: hydrate and run were not exercised: hydrate needs a server-rendered root stamp and run has no host-controlled unmount; embed is the documented host lifecycle and is what the test uses.
No browser-side verification: happy-dom proves the runtime API and DOM dispatch path, not real-browser rendering, rAF pacing, or CSS token resolution.

Model preservation across reloads was not exercised; the @foldkit/vite-plugin is absent, so the runtime logged 'No response from @foldkit/vite-plugin... Starting without Model preservation.' This is a warning, not a failure.

The @role-model-router/foldkit-ui type declaration defect (bare `foldkit/...` imports in .d.ts) is worked around in the app tsconfig; the wrapper's own typecheck and d.ts rewrite are not fixed by this slice.

The app has no declared vitest/happy-dom/typescript devDependencies, and the workspace install/lockfile entry for the new importer is controller-owned, so `npm test` is only reproducible after that install.
The mount test is not wired into CI/turbo scripts; the new package has a `test` script but the controller must include the package in the workspace pipeline.
